items.stem: Why does the quality of training data matter so much for an AI model?

options.text: The model learns its patterns from the data, so poor or skewed data leads to poor or unfair results
options.rationale: Correct: models reflect the data they learn from.

options.text: Data quality does not affect the model at all
options.rationale: Data quality strongly affects what the model learns.

options.text: Good data makes the computer physically faster
options.rationale: Data quality affects accuracy and fairness, not raw speed.

options.text: The model ignores the data it is given
options.rationale: The model learns directly from the data.

items.explanation: Correct: models reflect the data they learn from.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO problems can biased or incomplete training data cause? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Unfair results for groups missing from the data
options.rationale: Correct: missing groups can be treated unfairly.

options.text: Predictions that work badly on real, new examples
options.rationale: Correct: skewed data can make predictions unreliable.

options.text: The computer running out of electricity
options.rationale: Data bias does not drain electricity.

options.text: The screen changing colour by itself
options.rationale: Data bias does not change screen colours.

items.explanation: Correct: missing groups can be treated unfairly.

items.stem: An AI predicts well on its training examples but poorly on brand-new ones. What does this suggest?

options.text: It may have learned the training examples too closely and needs testing on new data
options.rationale: Correct: good training performance alone does not prove it generalises.

options.text: The AI is perfect and needs no testing
options.rationale: Poor results on new data show it is not reliable yet.

options.text: New data is not allowed in AI
options.rationale: Testing on new data is exactly what we should do.

options.text: Training data and new data are always identical
options.rationale: They differ, which is why testing on new data matters.

items.explanation: Correct: good training performance alone does not prove it generalises.
